description: The span contract of the Slen SDKs: one call, as an APM sees it, in the same shape whatever language wrote it. `fields` is the complete list, in the order the attributes are emitted — `field` is the property of the span object (`Slen\Sdk\Observability\SlenSpan` in PHP, `SlenSpan` in TypeScript), `attribute` the snake_case name it has in a log line or an OTLP attribute set, and the name of the field of `slen.SlenSpan` in Python, which names every field by its `attribute`; a null value is dropped, not sent (`false` is a value, and is sent). A span carries money, ids, a status, a duration and one yes/no — whether a flow run was answered from the cache — never a prompt, a message, an input or an output: a field that could hold what was said to a model does not belong in this list, and every suite fails on a name that looks like one. `outcomes` is the closed vocabulary of `outcome`. `operations` is the closed list of the values of `operation` — the names a span is written under — each with the SDKs that write it; a call that is not in the list writes no span (the customers' calls and the webhooks write none). Every SDK builds its span tests from this file — change the file and the span type of every SDK in one round. The rules are in the AGENTS.md of each package.

fields.holds: the SDK call that produced the span — one of `operations`
what happened, in one word — one of `outcomes`
the status of the run the call answered with or ended on: `queued`, `waiting`, `running`, `completed`, `rejected`, `failed`, `uncertain`; null when the call threw
wall clock around the call, transport retries included; for `executions.wait` the whole wait, pauses and every read

the flow run — the one the answer names, and on `executions.wait` the one the wait was asked about, so a wait that threw still says which run. It is also what money is counted by: one run can leave several spans (the submission, every wait on it, every replay of its key), and each repeats the `estimated` and `actual` the run had when the span was written — summed per span they overstate the run, taken once per `execution_id` they are its cost
the code of the operation the run was asked for: known before the call on `operations.execute` and `operations.execute_async`, read off the answer on `executions.wait`; what dashboards group by
what was estimated for the run's model calls, as a decimal string
what the run was charged once the fact was known, as a decimal string; null until its captures are in
the code of the error, or of the run that did not complete

whether the answer of a flow run came from the response cache (`cache.hit` of the run): true or false on the span of a run that has finished, null on every other span. True only for a run that completed with a stored answer as its `output`: a run that was rejected or broke carries no answer and says false, whatever its lookups found. The `usage` in a cached answer was spent by the run that produced it; `actual` is what this run itself was charged, null unless its flow called a model besides

outcomes.refused: the control plane said no — a decision, not a breakage: money (any 402, whichever ceiling), a policy (403 `policy_denied`, `model_not_allowed`, `customer_blocked`), a flow that rejected
outcomes.error: it broke, or was not let in: transport, provider, validation, a key that was refused (401, 403), the key's rate limit (429), anything else thrown — and a flow run that ended `failed` or `uncertain`, even when that arrived with a 200

operations.execute.means: a flow run submitted and walked inside the request; the status is the one the answer carries

operations.execute_async.means: a flow run handed to a worker (`execution_mode: async`). The span of a first submission says `queued`, and nothing has been charged when it is written; what the run came to is on the `executions.wait` span. A replayed idempotency key is answered with the run as it is now, and the span of that submission carries what it was answered with — the run's status, and when the run is over its outcome, `estimated`, `actual` and `cache_hit` as well: it may say `completed` and a cost. The name is the call's, not the answer's

executions.wait.means: a wait on a flow run, written once, when the wait ends — however many status reads it took. The status is the last state the wait read: the finished run, or the one still pending when the timeout was up (`outcome` is `ok` for that: a timeout of a wait is not a failure). `estimated`, `actual` and `cache_hit` are that state's: `actual` is there when the run's captures were in by the time the wait ended, and null otherwise — not known yet, or nothing was charged; the wait does not go on reading for it. A wait that threw is `error` (or `refused`), with `execution_id`. A single status read (`executions.get`) writes no span
